SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r1.claim: The surah contrasts restricted, partial shaping of fingertips with the unrestricted, general shaping of creation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r1.anchor: وذكر نوعين من التسوية: تسوية جزئية مقيدة وهي تسوية البنان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r2.claim: It names two stages of human creation, the semen drop and the clot.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r2.anchor: وذكر طورين من أطوار خلق الإنسان، وهما النطفة والعلقة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r4.claim: God is described with plural forms such as We are able, We gather, and We shape, as well as singular forms such as He created and proportioned.

NAHHAS:v5p92/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p92/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p92/r17.claim: God created him and fashioned him as a speaking, hearing, seeing human.
NAHHAS:v5p92/r17.anchor: أي فخلقه الله جل وعز فسواه بشرا ناطقا سميعا بصيرا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r4.claim: The agent is omitted from left aimless, created, fashioned, and made, matching the preceding passive and the sūra’s urgent tone.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r4.anchor: وعدم ذكر فاعل الخلق وما بعده مناسب لحذف فاعل الترك. وكل ذلك مناسب لجو العجلة في السورة

RAZI-FULL:v30p207#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p207#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p207#2/r1.claim: After being a drop, the human being became a clot.
RAZI-FULL:v30p207#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : { ثم كان علقة } أي الإنسان كان علقة بعد النطفة

RAZI-FULL:v30p207#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p207#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p207#2/r2.claim: One interpretation is that God created, apportioned, and proportioned the human being.

RAZI-FULL:v30p207#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p207#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v30p207#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil say “created” means breathed the spirit into him, while “proportioned” means completed his limbs.
RAZI-FULL:v30p207#2/r3.anchor: فخلق ، أي فنفخ فيه الروح ، فسوى فكمل أعضاءه ، وهو قول ابن عباس ومقاتل

STUDYQURAN:75:37/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:37/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:37/r1.claim: The life stages from gestation to adulthood demonstrate God’s omnipotence, especially His power to resurrect.
STUDYQURAN:75:37/r1.anchor: This is one of several passages that cite the phases of life from gestation to adulthood as proof of God’s Omnipotence and especially of His ability to resurrect

TAB-FULL:v23p526#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p526#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p526#2/r1.claim: The denier of resurrection began as a small amount of semen in a man; this origin demonstrates God’s power to recreate after death.
TAB-FULL:v23p526#2/r1.anchor: ألم يك هذا المنكر قدرة الله على إحيائه من بعد مماته

TABATABAI:75:36-39/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r5.claim: The subject that becomes a clinging clot may be the human being or the semen.
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r5.anchor: أي ثم كان الإنسان - أو المني - قطعة من دم منعقد

TABATABAI:75:36-39/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r6.claim: God then measured and formed it with adjustment and completion.

TABRISI:75:37-40/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:37-40/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:37-40/r5.claim: The clot develops into a created form in the womb, which God fashions in its body and internal and external organs.
TABRISI:75:37-40/r5.anchor: { ثم كان علقة فخلق } منها خلقا في الرحم { فسوى } خلقه وصورته وأعضاءه الباطنة والظاهرة

TABRISI:75:37-40/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:37-40/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:75:37-40/r6.claim: Another view says God makes him a human after birth and completes his strength.
TABRISI:75:37-40/r6.anchor: وقيل: فسواه إنسانا بعد الولادة وأكمل قوته

TABRISI:75:37-40/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:37-40/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:75:37-40/r7.claim: A further gloss says God created bodies and proportioned them for actions, assigning each limb its own function.
TABRISI:75:37-40/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه فخلق الأجسام فسواها للأفعال وجعل لكل جارحة عملا يختص بها

BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r1.claim: After forty days the semen becomes, by God’s power, a thick, dark-red clinging clot, having been white fluid; the commentary links this sequence to 23:14.
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r1.anchor: أي ثم كان لمني بعد أربعين يوما قطعة دم جامد غليظ أحمر بقدرة الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r2.claim: After another forty days it becomes flesh capable of differentiation into organs; God makes bones, covers them with flesh to perfect form and prepare it for powers and the spirit, then proportionately fashions it.
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r2.anchor: جعلها مضغة مخلقة بعد أربعين أخرى أي قطعة لحم قابل لتفريق الأعضاء

BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r3.claim: فسوى means that God proportioned and perfected the creature’s formation.
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r3.anchor: فكسا العظام لحما يحسن به خلقه وتصويره

BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r4.claim: Kāshifī glosses the phrase as forming the person’s shape and limbs and breathing the spirit into him.
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r4.anchor: قال الكاشفي) : س رلست كردصورت واندام اورا وووح دردميد

BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r5.claim: The Mufradāt explains perfecting as making the creature’s formation conform to divine wisdom.
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r5.anchor: وفي المفرات جعل خلقه على ما اقتضته الحكمة الإلهية

BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r6.claim: Another view takes proportioning to mean matching each paired bodily organ with its counterpart.
BURSEVI:v10p199#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم : معنى التسوية والتعديل جعل كل عضو من أعضائه الزوج

THALABI:v10p92/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p92/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p92/r5.claim: The drop becomes a clinging clot; God then creates and proportionately forms it, making male and female.
THALABI:v10p92/r5.anchor: ثم كان علقة فخلق فسوى خلقه فجعل منه الزوجين الذكر والأنثى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r8.claim: God formed him from a clot into a complete human being.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r8.anchor: { ثم كان علقة فخلق فسوى } فخلقه الله فسوى خلقه، حتى صار إنسانا بعد أن كان علقة.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r4.claim: After recalling human creation, the surah ends by warning in a question that the power which created humans will also resurrect the dead.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:31/r4.anchor: bu gücün ölüleri de dirilteceğini bildiren uyarı âyetiyle sona ermektedir.

ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r8.claim: After recalling creation from a drop, the passage asks whether the one who formed the sexes is not capable of bringing the dead to life.
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r8.anchor: (أليس ذلك بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى (40)

ASAD-NOTES:75:36#n16/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:36#n16/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:36#n16/r1.claim: Asad refers readers to his notes on 87:2 and 91:7 for his rendering of sawwa; the following sentence breaks off after mentioning God's creating.
ASAD-NOTES:75:36#n16/r1.anchor: For this rendering of sawwa, see note 1 on 87:2 and note 5 on 91:7. The stress on God's creating

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p29/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p29/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p29/r1.claim: Quranic word placement is precise: general ordering patterns and local context shape which expression comes first.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p29/r1.anchor: إن القرآن الكريم دقيق في وضع الألفاظ ورصفها بجنب بعض دقة عجيبة فقد تكون له خطوط عامة في التقديم والتأخير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p480/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p480/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p480/r1.claim: Quranic word order may follow chronological priority in existence, while particular contexts and overall coherence can also call for a given ordering.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p480/r1.anchor: إن القرآن كما ذكرت يقدم الألفاظ ويؤخرها حسبما يقتضيه المقام فقد يكون سياق الكلام مثلاً متدرجاً حسب القدم والأولية في الوجود

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r1.claim: Taṣrīf means change or variation; the same root describes changes in word forms in Arabic morphology.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r1.anchor: التصريف هو التغيير (وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاء وَالأَرْضِ لآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ (164) البقرة) تغييرها من جهة لأخرى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r2.claim: The Quran uses taṣrīf to present a single issue in varied forms and examples until the evidence becomes clear.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r2.anchor: فالتصريف التغيير يأتي للمسألة الواحدة ويذكرها بصور شتى يغيّر فيها حتى يوصلها لك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r3.claim: Resurrection is demonstrated through the revival of dead earth as a preparatory example, including 41:39.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r3.anchor: إثبات الحياة بعد الموت، هذه مسألة، كيف يتوصل إليها؟ يتوصل لها بإحياء الأرض بعد موتها كمثال تمهيدي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r4.claim: The Quran also reasons from human development from semen through a clinging clot and formation, including the creation of male and female, to God's power to resurrect.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r4.anchor: أحياناً يستدل بالحياة الآخرة على خلق الإنسان وتطوره (أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَنِيٍّ يُمْنَى (37) ثُمَّ كَانَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّى (38)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r6.claim: God can re-create the dead, having first made man from a sperm drop, perfected him, and granted him various abilities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r6.anchor: it was the Almighty Who created him from a drop of sperm and perfected him and blessed him with various abilities.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r5.claim: The sūrah ends where it began: after discussing arrogance and Judgement, it returns to the opening doubt about resurrection in 75:3–4 and asks whether a person will be left unaccountable.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r5.anchor: Here in these verses, the sūrah ends on the subject with which it began.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r6.claim: He frames leaving people unaccountable as a violation of God’s justice and wisdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r6.anchor: if leaving him unaccountable is against the justice and wisdom of the

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r1.claim: The passive description of the fluid being poured points to the act’s lack of attention or elaborate arrangement by the person who emits it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r1.anchor: points to a lack of attention and any elaborate arrangement.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r2.claim: Providence guides the fluid through stages in darkness: it becomes a clot, is shaped, perfected, and finally emerges male or female.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r2.anchor: The drop of fluid becomes a clot of blood.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r3.claim: Because only providence fashions the human being through these stages, its abundant signs of power, wisdom, and creativity show that God can recreate the dead.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r3.anchor: is amply capable of recreating him once he dies.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r4.claim: The creator alone forms and molds the person; no one else has a role in development from the fluid to a perfected man or woman.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p85/r4.anchor: no one else has any ro le in

ALUSI-FULL:v29p150/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150/r1.claim: By God’s power the drop became a clot, as in the cited account of embryonic stages; He fashioned it and proportioned and completed it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p150/r1.anchor: أي بقدرة الله تعالى كما قال تعالى ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة فخلق أي فقدر الله عز وجل بأن جعلها سبحانه مخلقة فسوى فعدل وكمل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r5.claim: God places a soul in the embryo and then forms it proportionately.

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:37-39/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:37-39/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:37-39/r2.claim: He became a clot; God then created and proportioned him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:37-39/r2.anchor: ثم كان علقة فخلق فسوى } فقدره فعدله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r3.claim: The particle of distance marks the astonishing greatness of the transformation and also temporal delay.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r3.anchor: أشار إليه بأداة البعد مع إفادتها للتراخي في الزمان أيضا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r4.claim: A ʿalaqa is fresh, bright-red, intensely red and thick blood.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r4.anchor: أي دما أحمر عبيطا شديد الحمرة والغلظة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r5.claim: God then determines and forms the person's flesh, bones, nerves, and other substances and attributes.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r5.anchor: قدر سبحانه عقب ذلك لحمه وعظامه وعصبه وغير ذلك من جواهره وأعراضه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r6.claim: He proportioned the result into another creation, a fully adjusted, independent person.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r6.anchor: أي عدل عن ذلك خلقا آخر غاية التعديل شخصا مستقلا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r9.claim: God does not abandon the drop, clot, morsel, or bones, but carries each stage through to a complete new creation in accord with manifest wisdom.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r9.anchor: كما لم يترك النطفة حتى صيرها علقة ولا ترك العلقة حتى صيرها مضغة ولا ترك المضغة حتى صيرها عظاما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p340/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p340/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p340/r9.claim: Taswiyah means straightening and making creation precise; restoring the fingertips finely is a metonym for creating them, since nothing is made well-proportioned without being recreated.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.speaker: جمهور المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.claim: Most interpreters say the entire passage concerns Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.anchor: قال جمهور المتأولين: هذه الآية كلها إنما نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r6.claim: An alaqa is a piece of blood, since blood is called alaq.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r6.anchor: القطعة من الدم، لأن الدم هو العلق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r7.claim: God formed the human from semen as a composite of different elements and proportioned him into an independent person.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فخلق فسوى معناه فخلق الله منه بشرا مركبا من أشياء مختلفة فسواه شخصا مستقلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r8.speaker: مصحف ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r8.claim: Ibn Masud's codex has يخلق in the imperfect tense.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p426/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p426/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p426/r1.claim: After the sperm drop he became a clinging clot; God then breathed a spirit into him and fashioned his creation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p426/r1.anchor: ثم كان علقة بعد النطفة فخلق فيه الروح وسوى خلقه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r5.claim: The drop becomes a clot and then a morsel, is shaped and receives the spirit, becoming a sound, complete human by God's permission and decree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r5.anchor: أي: فصار علقة، ثم مضغة، ثم شكل ونفخ فيه الروح، فصار خلقا آخر سويا سليم الأعضاء،

JISHUMI:v10p7196/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r3.speaker: الحسن، وأبو عمرو، وحفص عن عاصم، ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, and Yaʿqūb read yumnā with yāʾ, following al-manī; the rest read it with tāʾ, following al-nuṭfah, as Abū Ḥātim prefers, while Abū ʿUbayd prefers yāʾ.
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r3.anchor: قرأ الحسن وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب: يمنى بالياء

JISHUMI:v10p7196/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r6.claim: ʿAlaqah is a piece of congealed blood.

JISHUMI:v10p7196/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r15.claim: The semen becomes a clot; God then creates and forms the person, including internal and external organs, in the womb.
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r15.anchor: صار المني علقة فخلق، ثم خلق منه الخلق فسوى خلقه وصوره

JISHUMI:v10p7196/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r16.claim: Another explanation says God proportioned the clot into a human being as people observe.
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r16.anchor: وقيل: سواه إنسانا على ما نشاهده

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r10.claim: After being a drop of semen, the human becomes a clinging clot.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r10.anchor: يعني أنه كان بعد النطفة علقة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r11.claim: One possibility is that God creates him in the womb before birth, then proportions him after birth as strength and movement mature.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r11.anchor: خلق من الأرحام قبل الولادة وسوي بعدها عند استكمال القوة وتمام الحركة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r12.claim: Another possibility is that God creates bodies and fits them for action, assigning each limb its function.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r12.anchor: خلق الأجسام وسواها للأفعال , فجعل لكل جارحة عملا

MUQATIL:75:34-40/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r5.claim: After the semen drop became a clot, God created and fashioned the human being.
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r5.anchor: { ثم كان } بعد النطفة { علقة فخلق فسوى } [آية: 38] الله خلقه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#15/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#15/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#15/r1.claim: After forty days the semen becomes a solid clot of blood; God then creates and forms a human being upright.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#15/r1.anchor: بعد اربعين يوما ﴿ فخلق فسوى ﴾ فخلق الله منه بشرا سويا

QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r8.claim: The ʿalaqa is blood after the nutfa; the sequence shows God’s ordering from a lowly origin.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r8.anchor: أي دما بعد النطفة، أي قد رتبه تعالى بهذا كله على خسة قدره

QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r9.claim: Fa-khalaqa means determined; fa-sawwā means fashioned and proportioned, placing the spirit within.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r9.anchor: أي فسواه تسوية، وعدله تعديلا، يجعل الروح فيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p665/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p665/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p665/r1.claim: He created and determined the human being, then proportioned him perfectly.

TAB-FULL:v23p527/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p527/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p527/r1.claim: The human develops from a drop to a clot, then God forms him into a complete, speaking, hearing, seeing person.
TAB-FULL:v23p527/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: أليس الذي فعل ذلك فخلق هذا الإنسان من نطفة

TABRISI:75:26-28/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:26-28/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:26-28/r12.claim: An ʿalaqa is a clotted piece of blood.
